items.heading: 1 Before the MBA
items.text: 1 Before the MBA or in the first term: fill genuine background gaps If you are coming from a non-finance or non-quant background into a finance specialization, or a non-technical background into an analytics-heavy track, a short foundational course (Excel modeling basics, statistics fundamentals) before or in term one prevents you from drowning in core coursework later.

items.heading: 3 in the Final Term
items.text: 3 In the final term or right after: target the specific interview gap Once you know the exact roles you are interviewing for, this is when narrow, high-signal prep, case practice for consulting, a final modeling sprint for finance, PMP once you are eligible, pays off fastest, because it is aimed at a specific, known interview process rather than a general skill.

figures.label: Time Required
figures.source: Requires either a bachelor's degree plus 36 months of project-leading experience, or a high-school diploma plus 60 months, along with 35 hours of formal project management education, before you can sit the exam. Best suited to students who already have some project-leadership experience going into or during the MBA, not a fresh-MBA credential to chase from zero.
